# A gear you reach by contract can already be deployed; one you reach by `deps` cannot

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-referenced-gears`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

Two questions arrived together and are one question.

*How does a product avoid containing gears that are already running?* Most
integrations are not greenfield: a `types-registry` and an event broker are up,
several products share them, and adding a gear must not regenerate what is
already deployed. ADR-0016 decision 1 answered this and remains entirely
unbuilt — nothing in `crates/` mentions an installation, `product(...)` takes no
reference, `InclusionReason` has its three original variants.

*And what happens now that system gears ship their own deployment artefacts?*
[gears-rust#4663](https://github.com/constructorfabric/gears-rust/pull/4663)
(open, `feature/deploy`) adds a `platform-host` binary bundling the
trust-coupled core and system gears, a `toolkit-common` Helm library chart, a
`toolkit-platform` umbrella listing gears as conditional dependencies, per-gear
charts of five one-line templates over the library, and a parameterised
`oop-gear.Dockerfile`.

Read together, the PR answers the first question rather than complicating it.

### The rule that decides everything, and which ADR-0016 does not state

`deps` are **link-time**. `resolve/closure.rs`'s header records the finding: the
gear macro emits a hidden re-export per entry and the registry treats a missing
one as a hard `MissingDeps` failure, *"so a process containing a gear contains
everything that gear reaches"*.

It follows, with no room for preference, that:

> **A gear reached through `colocated_deps` must be compiled into the binary and
> therefore can never be "already deployed elsewhere". Only a gear reached
> across a contract edge can be.**

The platform arrived at the same line independently, which is the strongest
evidence available that it is the real one. `platform-host` bundles exactly the
`deps`-coupled cluster into one binary; the out-of-process gears are separate
pods reached over REST contracts through the `DirectoryService`. Link-time
coupling stays inside a binary; contract edges cross the pod boundary. Two
designs, arrived at separately, cutting in the same place.

### Where ADR-0016 has to be corrected

ADR-0016 says "already deployed" is expressed as **a reference to another
product's lock**, keyed by path, and argues it well: the lock exists, is
canonical, ordered, hashed, and records exactly what was resolved.

`platform-host` has no Gearbox lock. It is built and deployed by the platform's
own chart. The most important installation there will ever be cannot be pointed
at the way that ADR proposes. The reasoning was sound and the ground moved.

### What blocks it in the code

Verified by reading, not inferred:

* **`report_orphans` in `resolve/partition.rs` raises `GBX0311` as an error**
  for every closure member placed in no application — which is precisely the
  state a referenced gear creates. `ResolvedProduct::is_writable` is
  `!self.diagnostics.has_errors()`, so the lock is then refused. This is the
  single hardest blocker and ADR-0016 does not name it.
* **`provider_index` in `resolve/cuts.rs` is closure-only**, so a contract whose
  only provider is referenced has no provider at all: `GBX0404`.
* **`ResolvedBinding.provider_application` is not optional** (`ApplicationId`,
  not `Option<ApplicationId>`) and a referenced provider has no application.
  That is schema, not a check.
* **`generate/rust.rs` links every `application.gears` entry** through
  `link_idents()`, returning `UnlinkableIdent` when a root is not a declared
  dependency. A referenced gear that leaked into an application would be linked
  *and* deployed — the double-run hazard, visible only at runtime.

> **Citations here name functions and types, not line ranges.** ADR-0016 cites
> `structural.rs:212-228` for `GBX0301`, which is `check_grpc_without_hub`;
> `GBX0301` is raised in `resolve/closure.rs` and `validate.rs`. It also counts
> `ProductIntent`'s fields, and the count has been wrong for a while — it grows.
> Numbers in a document nobody recompiles go stale and then mislead, so this one
> gives none.

## Decision Outcome

### 1. An installation is declared. A lock is not required.

```
installation(
    id = "platform",
    at = "http://platform-host:50051",
    provides = ["api-contracts/PaymentApi@v1", "types-registry/TypesApi@v1"],
)
```

`at` is the `DirectoryService` the referenced side registers with — the PR's
`directoryEndpoint`. `provides` names the contracts it serves, **with versions**,
which is what makes skew refusable without a lock.

This supersedes ADR-0016's lock-path reference *as the mechanism*. Reading a
lock, where one exists, stays available as a later refinement that could derive
`provides` instead of restating it — it is not designed here, and an
installation that both declares `provides` and points at a lock is not a case
this ADR settles.

**Greenfield stays the default and stays byte-identical.** A product declaring
no installation resolves, generates and behaves exactly as today. That is a
constraint on the implementation, not an aspiration.

### 2. Only a contract edge may cross the boundary

A gear claimed by an installation that is *also* reached from a local gear's
`colocated_deps` is a contradiction: the local gear cannot link it and reference
it. That must be **refused with a diagnostic naming both the installation and
the depending gear**, not silently linked and not silently referenced.

This is the ADR's central constraint. Everything below is a consequence.

### 3. What a referenced gear contributes

It occupies the catalogue and satisfies contracts. It produces **no crate, no
application, no image, no chart** — so `generate`'s Docker and Helm paths, which
iterate `lock.applications`, are already correct and need no filter.

What must change:

* `GBX0311` gains an exemption for a referenced gear. Not a relaxation of the
  check — a gear that is neither placed nor referenced is still an error, and
  that is the case the check was written for.
* `provider_index` is seeded from the closure **and** from the installations'
  `provides`, and a classified edge records which side its provider came from.
* `ResolvedBinding` learns that a provider may be external. Whether that is
  `Option<ApplicationId>` or a variant is an implementation choice; the schema
  change is not.
* `InclusionReason` gains a variant. Its one exhaustive `match` is
  `resolve/product.rs`'s `explain_gears`, which needs a provenance edge — and
  there is no `NodeKind` for an installation today, so the explanation graph
  gains a node. That is the one place where this is a design question rather
  than a mechanical addition.

### 4. `check_grpc_without_hub` must learn about the installation

`resolve/structural.rs`'s `check_grpc_without_hub` raises `GBX0314` when an
application holds gRPC-registering gears and no hub. Under an installation the
hub is `platform-host`'s, so the first real use of this feature would produce a
red herring error. The check becomes: *no hub here and none reachable through an
installation*. `GBX0315`'s counterpart — a host with nothing to host — has the
mirror-image problem and the same answer.

### 5. The generated tree's deployment artefacts live under `deploy/`

`deploy/helm/...` and `deploy/docker/...`, rather than `helm/` and `docker/`
beside `apps/`. This matches the platform's own convention, which is the whole
reason to adopt it: one word means one thing in both repositories.

**`layout` and `deploy/` are two decisions, not one.** `product(layout = ...)`
names where the *crates* go and defaults to `apps/`; it must not move the
deployment artefacts as a side effect. A product that sets `layout = "processes"`
for an existing checkout still writes `deploy/`.

### 6. A referenced gear's `deploy/` is read for wiring, and for nothing else

A consumer needs the Service name and port to reach a referenced provider. Those
come from the referenced gear's own `deploy/`, not from `cluster_dns`, which
mints a DNS name for an application *this* product places and would be inventing
an address for something it does not deploy.

Gearbox never renders, copies or validates a foreign chart. It reads two facts
out of it.

### 7. Version skew across the boundary is its own refusal

The installation declares `PaymentApi@v1`; a new gear consumes `@v2`. Inside a
closure that is `GBX0405`, whose remedy is "select the provider" — useless here,
because the provider is deployed and not the integrator's to select.

A new code refuses it, naming both versions and the two remedies that are real:
**upgrade the installation, or take a gear built against the version it offers.**
This is the one place ADR-0013's "errors warn, they do not block" does not
reach — generating against a contract the other side does not serve produces a
binary that starts and then fails.

### 8. `GBX0411` is retired only after (3)

`resolve/bindings.rs`'s `report_unhonoured_endpoints` refuses every
`bind(endpoint = ...)` and its help text already promises this decision:
*"Pointing at a provider outside the product is not expressible yet"*. It must
not be retired before `provider_index` admits referenced providers, or an
endpoint is honoured for an edge that never classified.

ADR-0016's Traceability claims this retirement in the past tense. It has not
happened, and that claim is corrected there.

## Consequences

* **A second product in the corpus is still required**, as ADR-0016 said — but
  the *first* observable case is cheaper than it looked: a product that
  references the platform and builds one gear of its own. That does not need a
  second Gearbox product at all, only an installation declaration.
* **`provides` is restated, not derived**, and can therefore drift from what the
  installation actually serves. That is the price of not requiring a lock. The
  mitigation is that drift surfaces as a runtime failure the diagnostic in (7)
  cannot predict — and saying so is better than implying the declaration is
  checked.
* **The explanation graph gains a node kind**, so "why is this gear here" gains
  the answer "it is not; it is already running over there".
* **Two umbrella charts exist** — the platform's `toolkit-platform` and
  Gearbox's generated one. This ADR does not settle which deploys a product's
  gears, and that question is real.
* `LOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` moves when (3) lands.

## Confirmation

* The greenfield claim is the existing suite, unchanged: a product declaring no
  installation must generate byte-for-byte what it generates today.
* The `deps`-crossing refusal in (2) is confirmed on a fixture, because the
  corpus has no such contradiction to find.
* The referenced-gear claim is confirmed by resolving a product that references
  the platform and asserting: no application for the referenced gear, no crate,
  no chart, and a consumer wired to the Service name read from its `deploy/`.
* `GBX0314`'s exemption is confirmed by the case that would otherwise be a false
  positive: a local gRPC gear whose hub is in the installation.
* The skew refusal in (7) is confirmed on a fixture, since the corpus has no
  version disagreement.

## Traceability

* **Supersedes ADR-0016 decision 1** on the reference mechanism: an installation
  is declared rather than read out of another product's lock. ADR-0016's
  decisions 2, 3 and 4 have landed and are untouched.
* **Will relax** what `GBX0311` refuses (`resolve/partition.rs`,
  `report_orphans`) — future tense, deliberately.
* **Will retire** `GBX0411` (`resolve/bindings.rs`), after and not before the
  provider index admits referenced providers.
* Extends ADR-0002: what is read out of an installation is projected, never
  restated — which is exactly why `provides` restating contract versions is
  called out above as a cost rather than presented as a design.
* Respects ADR-0010: `gears-rust` is read, never written. A gear's `deploy/` is
  read for two facts.
* Depends on gears-rust#4663 for the shape it integrates with. That PR is open,
  and our corpus branch has no `deploy/` at all, so this ADR records the
  contract the two sides must share — Service name, port, config path,
  `<app>.enabled` — and not the chart internals.
* Leaves open, explicitly: whether Gearbox's generated per-application charts
  should become thin charts over `toolkit-common`. That belongs to the chart
  work after the PR merges.
